title: The Future of Hollywood Movie Draft
format: Sean, Amanda, and Chris Ryan read the consolidation tea leaves, then draft the talent, franchises, and studio lots they'd build a studio around. Plus: Sean talks documentary with Ross McElwee.

segments.heading: The State of Hollywood
segments.note: Mergers, loss leaders, and the year's two box-office stories

films.title: Top Gun: Maverick
films.note: David Ellison's one unambiguous Skydance hit, per Sean's grudging defense.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.note: Nolan's; the lone blockbuster-tier film they both admire this year, and a 'unicorn.'

films.title: You Can See Everything
films.note: Oppenheim/Fielder doc on Elizabeth Holmes; $100M and a Best Picture contender. Also discussed with McElwee.

films.title: Super Mario Galaxy
films.note: Fourth-biggest film of the year; neither enjoyed it.

films.title: Project Hail Mary
films.note: Cited as the encouraging mid-budget model.

films.title: Obsession
films.note: ~$500M sensation; held up as unreplicable rather than a template.

films.title: Backrooms
films.note: The other out-of-nowhere hit, paired with Obsession.

films.title: Resident Evil
films.note: CR's ideal template: a $60-80M budget, recognizable IP, a skilled director trusted to adapt it, and just one movie.

films.title: Avengers: Doomsday
films.note: Trailer dropped pre-taping; Amanda unmoved, Andy Greenwald texted at 7am that it 'got him.'

films.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
films.note: The generational-IP counterpoint to tired 50-year-old properties.

films.title: The Mandalorian and Grogu
films.note: Sean's example of spending too much on something that already feels like TV.

films.title: Wicker
films.note: Black Bear horror hit cited as proof smaller distributors can still break out.

films.title: Man of Tomorrow
films.note: Aaron Pierre attached.

films.title: Miami Vice 85
films.note: Michael B. Jordan splitting the top line with Austin Butler.

films.title: The Thomas Crown Affair
films.note: On Michael B. Jordan's slate.

films.title: Minecraft 2
films.note: Kirsten Dunst's for-the-kids paycheck.

films.title: Matchbox
films.note: Apple/Coogler; 'the cinematic event of the year,' per Amanda.

films.title: Exorcist: Martyrs
films.note: Early screenings reportedly disturbing.

films.title: La Bola Negra
films.note: Teased as next week's topic.

segments.heading: The Future of Hollywood Movie Draft
segments.note: Nine categories (actor, actress, and director each over and under 40, plus producer, franchise, and studio lot), with a die deciding each GM's backer. Sean draws shareholders, Amanda a loss-leader tech company, CR a benefactor. Sean's board: Pattinson, Scarlett Johansson, Aaron Pierre, Zendaya, Nolan, Cain Parsons, Kevin Feige, Batman, Warner Bros. Amanda's: DiCaprio, Kirsten Dunst, Chalamet, Emma Stone, Coogler, Lance Oppenheim, Amy Pascal, Bond, Sony. CR's: Ryan Gosling, Amanda Seyfried, Michael B. Jordan, Florence Pugh, Villeneuve, Curry Barker, Emma Thomas, X-Men, Pinewood. The films below are the résumés cited for the picks.

films.title: Marty Supreme
films.note: Chalamet's Oscar that didn't land; Amanda rides for it regardless.

films.title: Barbie
films.note: Gosling could plausibly return to it.

films.title: Materialists
films.note: Celine Song, the sleeper under-40 director; the divisive one Sean defended.

films.title: Foe
films.note: Aaron Pierre with Paul Mescal and Saoirse Ronan, one of 'the three people who saw it.'

films.title: Rebel Ridge
films.note: Pierre's calling card.

films.title: Fighting with My Family
films.note: Florence Pugh's wrestling movie (not Real Steel).

films.title: Real Steel
films.note: The robot-wrestling movie Sean doesn't want Pugh pivoting back to.

films.title: Creed
films.note: Michael B. Jordan's self-sustained franchise.

films.title: The Housemaid
films.note: Amanda Seyfried box-office gold; a sexed-up sequel floated.

films.title: Lovelace
films.note: Seyfried 'honored the character.'

films.title: Ted 2
films.note: Paired with In Time to show her range.

films.title: In Time
films.note: Seyfried and Timberlake; the broken-watches one.

films.title: The Adjustment Bureau
films.note: The hat-and-watches one, Matt Damon and Emily Blunt.

films.title: Civil War
films.note: 'The reason we have You Can See Everything,' because it made money for Alex Garland.

films.title: Logan
films.note: Dafne Keen's X-23, floated for Amanda's X-women.

films.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
films.note: Olivia Munn's Psylocke.

films.title: Don't Look Up
films.note: The odd one out on Leo's filmography.

films.title: Inception
films.note: The last sub-45 director DiCaprio worked with, Nolan.

films.title: One Battle After Another
films.note: DiCaprio; the loss-leader's 'just win Oscars every couple years' play.

films.title: Remake
films.note: His first film in 14 years; the aborted Hollywood adaptation of Sherman's March braided with his son Adrian's addiction and death.

films.title: Sherman's March
films.note: Restored at 40; the first-person documentary landmark, shaped mid-shoot into a portrait of women along the march route.

films.title: Backyard
films.note: The 40-minute experiment where he first melded observation with the autobiographical.

films.title: Primary
films.note: Drew, Leacock, and Pennebaker on JFK; the cinéma vérité touchstone he saw in a political science course.

films.title: Titicut Follies
films.note: Wiseman's first; a 'what not to do' that left him uneasy about the invisible camera.

films.title: Time Indefinite
films.note: A planned wedding film that pivoted into grief after his father's death and a miscarriage.

films.title: Bright Leaves
films.note: Tobacco and family, opened up by cousin John's Hollywood archive.

films.title: Bright Leaf
films.note: The Curtiz/Gary Cooper fiction film whose tobacco magnate may be modeled on McElwee's great-grandfather.

films.title: Photographic Memory
films.note: The earlier film featuring his son Adrian.

films.title: You Can See Everything
films.note: McElwee on his former student Oppenheim's doc: voyeurism, but with the subject's consent.
